plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure, aiming for steady, low-drawdown performance. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the mandate and reduce concentration.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to small positions (0.5% each).
Trim high-beta names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to reduce overall risk.
Buy ERY at 4% as a new, strong risk/reward long setup from the scanner.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential, with a focus on managing drawdown.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the mandate.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, along with a strong scanner setup. This approach carries substantially higher drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Sell high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) to near zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It maximizes exposure to income-generating ETFs and minimizes high-beta and leveraged positions. While aiming for reliable distributions, NAV can still fall in market downturns, and distributions are not guaranteed.
